spans.s: 1. श the first of the three sibilants (it belongs to the palatal class, but in sound as well as euphonic treatment often corresponds to ष्, though in some words pronounced more like स्).

1. ष the second of the three sibilants (it belongs to the cerebral class, and is sometimes substituted for स्, and more rarely for श्, and occasionally interchangeable with ख्; in sound it corresponds to sh in the English word shun; many roots which begin with स् are written in the Dhātu-pāṭha with ष्, prob. to show that their initial स् is liable to be cerebralized after certain prepositions).
2. ष mfn. (only L.; for 3. ष See below) best, excellent
3. ष mfn. = षष् ifc. (in पञ्च-ष, q.v.)
1. स the last of the three sibilants (it belongs to the dental class and in sound corresponds to s in sin).
3. स (in music) an abbreviated term for षड्-ज (see p. 1109, col. 2).
5. स mfn. (fr. √ सन्) procuring, bestowing (only ifc.; cf. पलु-ष॑ and प्रिय-स॑).

etym.s: [cf. Zd. hō, hā; Gk. ὁ, ἡ.]

spans.s: 7. स ind. (connected with सह, सम्, सम, and occasionally in BhP. standing for सह with instr.) an inseparable prefix expressing ‘junction’, ‘conjunction’, ‘possession’ (as opp. to अ priv.), ‘similarity’, ‘equality’

(and when compounded with nouns to form adjectives and adverbs it may be translated by ‘with’, ‘together or along with’, ‘accompanied by’, ‘added to’, ‘having’, ‘possessing’, ‘containing’, ‘having the same’ [cf. स-कोप, साग्नि, स-भाय, स-द्रोण, स-धर्मन्, स-वर्ण]; or it may = ‘ly’, as in स-कोपम्, ‘angrily’, सोपधि, ‘fraudulently’), RV.; &c.

etym.s: [cf. Gk. ἁ in ἁπλοῦς; Lat. sim in simplex; sem in semel, semper Eng. same.]
